dialogue.speaker: الموظف

dialogue.speaker: نور

dialogue.english: May God make up for it, God willing it'll work out, thanks.

lessons.culture: When something goes wrong, Iraqis say 'allah kareem' (God is generous) or 'in shaa2 allah tin7all' to stay calm and hopeful, and staff will often say 'laa tkhaaf' (don't worry). Speaking politely with 'law sama7t' gets help faster than raising your voice.

lessons.culture: Iraqis call opening hours "الدوام", the same word as working hours, so ask "شنو أوقات الدوام؟" before you set off. Big mosques in Baghdad welcome visitors outside prayer times: shoes come off at the door ("اشلع القندرة"), and women cover their hair and dress modestly.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; at the beach Iraqis ask for a "شمسيّة".

exercises.tip: A sun or beach umbrella is a "شمسيّة" in Iraqi speech; "مظلة" is understood too.

exercises.prompt: الجهّال ____ يبنون قلعة رمل (The children are building a sandcastle)
exercises.tip: "دا" before a verb means it is happening right now.

exercises.prompt: Translate: Where can we sit on the sand?

too_formal.feedback: "أين" and "نجلس" are formal; Iraqis say "وين نگعد".

exercises.tip: "نگعد" is we sit; the ق is said g.

exercises.prompt: Translate: I want to swim

too_formal.feedback: The "أن" is formal; Iraqis drop it.

exercises.tip: "أريد" is often shortened to "ريد" in quick speech.

exercises.prompt: Which one asks whether the water is cold?
Which one means "The waves are high today"?
Arrange: Do you have sunscreen? (to a man)

too_formal.item: هل معك كريم واقٍ من الشمس؟
too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "عندك كريم شمس؟".

too_formal.feedback: "جداً" is formal; Iraqis say "كلّش".

exercises.tip: "كلّش" is the Iraqi word for very.

reply.english: I have lots of things, go ahead and choose

reply.english: She'll surely like it, you have good taste

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, I want a souvenir for my family

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: كلّش طيّب! آخذ علبة. وشنو هذا العطر؟
dialogue.english: Very tasty! I'll take a box. And what is this perfume?

dialogue.speaker: Abu Khalid
dialogue.arabic: هذا عود طبيعي، ريحته كلّش حلوة
dialogue.english: This is natural oud, its scent is lovely

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.english: And is this box handmade?

dialogue.speaker: Samer
dialogue.arabic: أريد سجّادة صلاة هم. إذا أشتري ثنين، تنطيني بسعر أرخص؟

dialogue.english: I want a prayer rug too. If I buy two, will you give me a lower price?

pair.arabic: إذا أشتري ثنين، تنطيني بسعر أرخص؟
pair.transliteration: itha ashtiri thneen, tin6eeni b-si3ir arkhaS?
pair.english: Will you give me a lower price if I buy two?

response.english: As you wish, I'll take a bit off for you

pair.english: Can you wrap it as a gift?

lessons.culture: In Baghdad visitors buy gifts in the old markets: copper trays in Souq al-Safafeer, and dates, spices and cloth in al-Shorja. Iraqi dates such as برحي and خستاوي are a favourite gift, sellers often let you taste first, and gentle bargaining is answered with "تدلّل" or "على عيني".

exercises.prompt: You ask the seller: "تگدر تلفّه هديّة؟". He says "with pleasure". What does he say?

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; an Iraqi seller says "على عيني" or "تدلّل".

exercises.tip: "على عيني" (lit. on my eye) is a warm Iraqi yes.

exercises.prompt: You say: "هاي هديّة لأمّي، إن شاء الله تعجبها". The seller reassures you. What does he say?

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "أكيد تعجبها".

exercises.tip: "ذوگ" is taste, with the Iraqi g for ق.

exercises.prompt: هذا شغل ____؟ (Is this handmade?)

too_formal.feedback: Correct but bookish; Iraqis say "شغل إيد".

exercises.tip: "شغل إيد" (hand work) is the everyday way to say handmade.

exercises.prompt: إذا أشتري ثنين، ____ بسعر أرخص؟ (Will you give me a lower price if I buy two?)

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "تنطيني بسعر أرخص".

exercises.tip: "تنطيني" is the Baghdad form of "تعطيني", give me.

exercises.prompt: Translate: I want a silk scarf for my sister

too_formal.feedback: "وشاح" is formal; Iraqis say "شال".

exercises.prompt: Translate: I want a small bottle of oud oil

too_formal.item: أريد زجاجة صغيرة من دهن العود
too_formal.feedback: "زجاجة" is formal; Iraqis say "قنينة" or "غرشة".

exercises.tip: A bottle is "قنينة" or "غرشة" in Iraqi speech.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "This wooden box is beautiful"?
exercises.tip: "صندوگ" is a box or chest, with the Iraqi g.

exercises.prompt: Which one asks the seller if he has good dates?
Arrange: I want a box of spices as a gift

too_formal.feedback: Fine too; the plain form "هديّة" at the end is more natural.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I want a prayer rug

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "أريد".

exercises.tip: "سجّادة" is a rug; "سجّادة صلاة" is a prayer rug.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله على السلامة يا رنا! شلونها السفرة؟
dialogue.transliteration: il-7amdu lillaah 3ala is-salaama ya rana! shloonha is-safra?
dialogue.english: Welcome back, Rana, thank God you're safe! How was the trip?

dialogue.speaker: Rana
dialogue.arabic: كلّش حلوة، انبسطنا هواية، ورجعنا سالمين الحمد لله
dialogue.transliteration: kullish 7ilwa, inbisa6na hwaaya, w-rja3na saalmeen il-7amdu lillaah
dialogue.english: Really lovely, we had a great time, and we came back safe, thank God

dialogue.speaker: Omar

dialogue.speaker: Rana

dialogue.transliteration: ee, baawi3! il-ba7ar chaan kullish haadi
dialogue.english: Yes, look! The sea was very calm

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Really nice. Send me the photos on my phone

pair.english: Where are you going this holiday?

response.english: I'm going to travel to the sea
Really lovely, we had a great time

pair.english: Can you take a photo of us?
We came back safe, thank God

response.english: Thank God for your safe return

lessons.culture: Iraqi families usually travel together, and someone back from a trip is greeted with "الحمد لله على السلامة". Photos are sent straight away with "دزّلي الصور"; asking a stranger to take a group photo is fine, but photographing other families, especially women, without asking is not.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: "رجعنا سالمين، الحمد لله". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "الحمد لله على السلامة".

exercises.tip: This is the standard welcome for anyone back from a journey.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks you: "شلونها السفرة؟". Say it was really lovely and you had a great time.

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "انبسطنا هواية".

exercises.prompt: ____ الصور عالتلفون (Send me the photos on my phone)

too_formal.feedback: "أرسل" is formal; Iraqis say "دزّلي".

exercises.tip: "دز" is the Iraqi verb for send; to a woman "دزّيلي".

exercises.prompt: البحر ____ هادي (The sea is very calm)

too_formal.feedback: "جداً" is formal; Iraqis say "كلّش".

exercises.tip: "كلّش" comes before the adjective, like very.

exercises.prompt: Translate: We are travelling with the whole family

too_formal.feedback: "سـ" and "مع" are formal; Iraqis say "راح نسافر ويّا".

exercises.prompt: Translate: Can you take a photo of us? (to a man)

too_formal.item: هل تستطيع أن تلتقط لنا صورة؟
too_formal.feedback: This is formal; Iraqis say "تگدر تصوّرنا؟".

exercises.prompt: Which one asks how long someone's holiday is?
exercises.tip: "شگد" is how much or how long.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "What a beautiful view!"?
exercises.tip: "شنو" can start an exclamation as well as a question.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: We booked a house near the beach

too_formal.feedback: "قرب" is formal; Iraqis say "يم".

exercises.tip: "يم" is the Iraqi word for next to or near.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I will take my camera with me

too_formal.feedback: "سـ" and "معي" are formal; Iraqis say "راح" and "وياي".

challenge.title: Book a Trip and Handle a Problem
challenge.instructions: اكتب حوار قصير: احجز غرفة بفندق او تذكرة سفر، وبعدين صارت مشكلة (تأخير، شنطة ضايعة، او فاتتك الرحلة) وگول شلون حليتها.
required_elements: طلب حجز او تذكرة بجملة كاملة

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: هلا، اريد احجز تذكرة باص للبصرة
dialogue.transliteration: hala, areed a7jiz tathkira baas lil-basra
dialogue.english: Hello, I want to book a bus ticket to Basra.

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.transliteration: thihaab bass low thihaab w iyaab?
dialogue.english: One-way or round trip?

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: Round trip, how much is the price?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: ثلاثين ألف دينار، والباص يطلع الساعة تسعة
dialogue.transliteration: thalaatheen alif deenaar, w il-baas y6la3 is-saa3a tis3a
dialogue.english: Thirty thousand dinars, and the bus leaves at nine.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.arabic: للأسف فاتني الباص، اكو باص ثاني؟
dialogue.transliteration: lil-asaf faatni l-baas, aku baas thaani?
dialogue.english: Unfortunately I missed the bus, is there another one?

dialogue.speaker: الموظف
dialogue.arabic: لا تخاف، اكو باص بعد ساعتين
dialogue.transliteration: laa tkhaaf, aku baas ba3d saa3teen
dialogue.english: Don't worry, there's a bus in two hours.

dialogue.speaker: سامر
dialogue.english: May God make up for it, thanks a lot.
